prompt:
A hand-painted map of a vast cavern country: galleries, sunken rivers, salt flats and lightless lakes, lit faintly from within seen from directly above, in the manner of a painted fantasy map such as a map of Middle-earth: coastlines, mountain ranges drawn as shaded ridges, rivers as fine dark lines running downhill to the sea, forests as textured masses, marsh, desert and open plain each in its own tone. Oil on parchment in a 19th-century academic manner with a smooth, finely blended surface, soft glazed transitions, fine detail, no heavy impasto. Palette of umber, ochre, gold, olive and sea-green with near-black shading. Less detail at larger scale; nothing drawn smaller than a hill or a wood; no settlements, no roads, no figures, no borders between countries. No text, no lettering, no compass rose, no scale bar, no frame, no grid, not photographic. The whole sheet is land and sea; nothing is cut off at the edges.

On a square sheet, north at the top, almost all of it unbroken dark rock. In the north-east quarter only, one long cut gallery runs from north-west to south-east for about a tenth of the sheet's width, straight in its stretches, with a few side chambers, a stair at its north-western end and a round vault at its south-eastern end. Nothing else is hollow.
